annotation.authors_or_issuer: Leineweber, M.; Keusgen, C.V.; Bubeck, M.; Haltaufderheide, J.; Ranisch, R.; Klingler, C.
key_provisions_or_claims: Screened 1,518 publications and included 248 on ethics of social robots in elderly care.
Organises findings into ethical hazards, opportunities and unsettled questions, with at least 60 ethical aspects across three stakeholder groups.
Many issues are only marginally recognised, e.g. autonomy, deception, data protection, loss of human touch and liability gaps.
Notes that no pertinent standards exist for social robots in care settings.
Decision-makers need contextual evaluation of implementation scenarios and an understanding of the ethical discourse.
annotation.summary_en: Systematic qualitative review of 248 publications on the ethics of social robots in elderly care. It maps ethical hazards, opportunities and unsettled questions across three stakeholder groups. It is purely descriptive and aims to support decision-makers, who need contextual evaluation of implementation scenarios.
annotation.title_clean: Ethical Aspects of the Use of Social Robots in Elderly Care -- A Systematic Qualitative Review
annotation.title_en: Ethical Aspects of the Use of Social Robots in Elderly Care -- A Systematic Qualitative Review
